hyperedges.label: Server-Side Apply Logic Behind the Thin Extension

nodes.label: Public Multi-User SaaS (consent sign-up, email verification, ADMIN_EMAILS admin role)
nodes.norm_label: public multi-user saas (consent sign-up, email verification, admin_emails admin role)

nodes.label: SMTP Email Delivery via SMTP_URL
nodes.rationale: Any SMTP server works; without SMTP_URL, links are printed to the server log instead.

nodes.label: Mandatory Pre-Launch Preview
nodes.rationale: The user unticks listings and confirms before launch; filtered-out listings are shown with their reason, criteria can be edited and re-run, and listings with an unknown experience level stay in, flagged 'level tidak diketahui'.

nodes.label: Daily Cap of 25 Applications per Portal Account
nodes.norm_label: daily cap of 25 applications per portal account
nodes.rationale: Admin-configurable; overflow waits for the next day (Asia/Jakarta).

nodes.label: AutoJobs Extension Icon (128px)
nodes.description: 128x128 browser-extension icon: bold white checkmark centered on a solid royal-blue rounded square, flat style with no text or gradients, built to stay legible at small toolbar sizes.

nodes.label: Popup Pairing Form (AutoJobs address + pairing code)
nodes.norm_label: popup pairing form (autojobs address + pairing code)

nodes.label: Popup Portal Login Status and Check (Periksa login portal)
nodes.norm_label: popup portal login status and check (periksa login portal)

nodes.label: Popup Screenshot-Proof Opt-In (all-sites permission)
nodes.rationale: Saving screenshots as proof needs the optional access-to-all-sites permission, so it is an explicit user opt-in.

nodes.label: Checkmark Completion Motif
nodes.rationale: A checkmark reads as 'done/submitted', which matches the product's job auto-apply purpose; the flat, high-contrast white-on-blue design stays recognizable when shrunk to toolbar size.

nodes.label: Dedicated AutoJobs Work Window
nodes.rationale: Each job is opened, filled and submitted in a dedicated window; when a portal shows a CAPTCHA or verification step the extension brings the window forward and waits for the user.

nodes.label: Dry Run (Uji coba) Launch Option
nodes.rationale: Validation mode that fills every form but never clicks submit, so portal flows can be checked before live use.

nodes.label: Extension Pairing Flow (pairing code)
nodes.rationale: A pairing code created under Koneksi Portal links the browser extension to the user's AutoJobs account; the user then signs in to the portals in that same browser and keeps it open while a campaign runs.

nodes.label: Application Proof Capture (confirmation text, HTML snapshot, optional screenshots)
nodes.norm_label: application proof capture (confirmation text, html snapshot, optional screenshots)
nodes.rationale: Screenshots are only taken if the user grants 'access to all sites' in the extension popup, because Chrome's screenshot API needs it; proof files are deleted after the retention period.

nodes.label: Visibility-Gated Apply Queue (work window must stay visible)
nodes.norm_label: visibility-gated apply queue (work window must stay visible)
nodes.rationale: Chrome stops rendering covered or minimized windows, so while the AutoJobs work window is hidden the queue waits instead of burning attempts, and resumes on its own once the window is visible again.

nodes.label: First Real Run per Portal (dry-run validation)
nodes.norm_label: first real run per portal (dry-run validation)
nodes.rationale: Real apply forms sit behind each portal's login, so the apply patterns were written from public knowledge and checked only against the fake portal; small dry-run campaigns plus the Laporan timeline and HTML snapshot show where a flow stopped so the adapter can be adjusted before live use.

nodes.label: Never Bypass CAPTCHAs, 2FA or Bot Checks (human handoff policy)
nodes.norm_label: never bypass captchas, 2fa or bot checks (human handoff policy)
nodes.rationale: By design AutoJobs never solves or bypasses CAPTCHAs, 2FA or bot checks, never disguises automation, never stores portal passwords and never guesses answers to screening questions; the user completes verification steps.

nodes.label: docker-compose.yml — MVP Deployment Stack
nodes.rationale: Applying runs in users' browsers through the AutoJobs extension, so the server stack is only PostgreSQL, the web app (Next.js + extension API), the worker and Caddy for HTTPS.

nodes.label: caddy Service (automatic HTTPS reverse proxy)
nodes.rationale: Reverse-proxies DOMAIN to web:3000 and terminates TLS automatically.

nodes.label: postgres Service (postgres:17-alpine)
nodes.rationale: Port published only on 127.0.0.1 (PG_PORT, default 5432) for local development; a pg_isready healthcheck gates web and worker startup.

nodes.label: web Service (Next.js + extension API)
nodes.rationale: Runs database migrations on every start (npm run migrate && npm start).

nodes.label: worker Service (searches, recovery, retention)
nodes.rationale: stop_grace_period of 1m lets a running search finish before shutdown.

nodes.label: x-app Shared App Service Template (YAML anchor)
nodes.norm_label: x-app shared app service template (yaml anchor)

nodes.label: AutoJobs Browser Extension (Chrome/Edge, Manifest V3)
nodes.rationale: Applying runs in the user's own browser, with their own portal logins and internet connection, because portals' Cloudflare checks reject server-side automated browsers; the server therefore stores no portal passwords, sessions or cookies. For public distribution it goes to the Chrome Web Store with the localhost/127.0.0.1 host permissions removed.

nodes.label: Not in This Build (PRD P1/P2, later phases)
nodes.norm_label: not in this build (prd p1/p2, later phases)

nodes.label: Glints
nodes.rationale: Auto-apply supported in Phase 1; its search pages are loaded by the extension because Glints only answers a real browser the user has verified.

nodes.label: JobStreet
nodes.rationale: Auto-apply supported in Phase 1; searched by the worker over plain HTTPS; sign-in uses a one-time code sent by email.

nodes.label: LinkedIn
nodes.rationale: Search-only in Phase 1 (applications recorded as manual); Easy Apply is deferred to Phase 2.

nodes.label: Worker Process (campaign searches, crash recovery, retention)
nodes.norm_label: worker process (campaign searches, crash recovery, retention)
nodes.rationale: JobStreet and LinkedIn are searched over plain HTTPS; Glints pages are loaded by the extension instead because Glints only answers a real browser the user has verified.

nodes.label: AutoJobs README — Job Auto-Apply System (Phase 1 MVP)
nodes.norm_label: autojobs readme — job auto-apply system (phase 1 mvp)

nodes.label: Random 120–180 s Gap per Portal Account
nodes.norm_label: random 120–180 s gap per portal account
nodes.rationale: Applied per portal account so different portals run side by side; admin-configurable with a 120 s floor.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL as Data Store and Persistent Queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
nodes.norm_label: postgresql as data store and persistent queue (for update skip locked)
nodes.rationale: Lean stack with no Redis: claimNextForUser locks the next due item with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so a portal account never has two attempts at once and the 120–180 s gap holds even with several browsers paired.

nodes.label: Thin-Executor Extension Pattern
nodes.rationale: Portal patterns (adapters), answers (apply-plan), the gap, daily caps, retries and result handling live on the server, so fixing a portal means editing its adapter file with no extension update.

nodes.label: appdata Volume (encrypted CVs and proofs at DATA_DIR=/data)
nodes.norm_label: appdata volume (encrypted cvs and proofs at data_dir=/data)

nodes.label: Encrypted File Storage for CVs and Proofs (ENCRYPTION_KEY)
nodes.norm_label: encrypted file storage for cvs and proofs (encryption_key)
nodes.rationale: ENCRYPTION_KEY must be backed up: without it, stored CVs and proof files can't be read.

nodes.label: Extension End-to-End Test (Playwright + Microsoft Edge)
nodes.rationale: Runs in Edge because branded Chrome no longer loads unpacked extensions from the command line, and is skipped when Edge isn't installed; it applies against a fake JobStreet-style Quick Apply portal.
